My research develops statistical learning methods that are interpretable and
computationally efficient, often together with colleagues who bring the data
and the questions. Each of the five lines of work below has a story that
tells how it developed. The stories distinguish the methods developed with my
colleagues, such as NeSSC, TORS and PARSEG, from existing methods, such as
topic models and GAITD regression, that we applied to new problems. Other
topics and funded projects follow. The
[Publications](publications.qmd) page shows how these lines developed over time,
with the complete list of works.

## From methods to real-world problems {#applications}

The methods of the five lines below have been applied in many fields, from
tourism and transport to health and botany. The diagram is drawn from the
publications of each line.

## Funded projects {#projects}

### Principal investigator and scientific coordinator

::: {.plain-list}
- **Clustering in non-Euclidean spaces: theoretical foundations and alternative
  approaches.** Principal investigator. Fondazione di Sardegna, call for basic
  research projects 2025.
- **HEALTH-GUARD: analysis of the environmental, economic and social
  sustainability impacts of the processes studied in the LucAS project.**
  Scientific coordinator for the University of Cagliari. Part of the project
  *LucAS – Lucani tra Ambiente e Salute*, funded by the Basilicata Region.
- **The role of advanced statistics in the co-planning of interventions
  supporting non-self-sufficiency.** Scientific coordinator. Funded by the
  Italian National Social Security Institute (INPS), call of 15 July 2020.
:::

### Research units

I am or have been a senior member of the University of Cagliari units of
national and regional projects, including *RISING* (National Programme for
Research, Innovation and Competitiveness 2021–2027), *e.INS – Ecosystem of
Innovation for Next Generation Sardinia* and *GRINS – Growing Resilient,
Inclusive and Sustainable* (National Recovery and Resilience Plan), and
projects funded by the Ministry of University and Research, the Fondazione di
Sardegna, the Autonomous Region of Sardinia and the Ethereum Foundation.
